raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this. I've got 163 mu spread across a lot of different things, and I need to figure out how to manage all of it without running out of cash or labor.

The way I see it, my 80 mu of wheat-maize is my bread and butter — that's what the family depends on. The cotton on the western plot is a gamble every year but prices have been okay. The stevia I sell on contract so that's reliable income. The vegetables — watermelon, broccoli, chili — those are smaller plots, high value if I manage them right, but they eat up time.

My biggest worry this year is labor. My brother-in-law took a construction job in Baoding, so my wife and my father are the ones helping me full-time. My father's getting slower. At wheat harvest I need to hire people and get the combine in, then immediately turn around and get maize planted — that week in June is the most stressful of the year. Cotton picking in September is the other bottleneck. I'll need hired hands for both.

For wheat, I always put down compound fertilizer before seeding and then top up with urea at jointing if the plants look pale. The extension guy told me last year I should do 15 kg N total per mu, but after that drought year when I cut back and the yield dropped to 380 kg, I've been keeping it at 17 kg to be safe. Irrigation I'll do four times — before planting to wet the soil, at tillering, at jointing, and at heading. If spring rains come early I'll skip the last one.

For maize, I go straight in after wheat with minimal tillage — there's no time to plow. I use a local no-till planter I hire by the day. I only irrigate once if there's no rain in August. Last year I got 490 kg/mu and was happy with that.

Cotton is the headache crop. 40 mu is as much as I want to manage. The bollworm was terrible last year — I ended up spraying five times. This year I'll watch the traps earlier and try to catch it before it gets bad. Three fertilizer splits: base before planting, once when boll formation starts, and a light foliar spray in late season. I'll apply about 13 kg N per mu total.

Stevia is easy money. I have a contract with the buying station, they give me a planting guide and I follow it. 20 mu, transplant in early May, three leaf harvests through the season. The main cost is the transplants and some fertilizer. They're reliable buyers.

Watermelon on 8 mu — I use plastic mulch and plant in mid-April. Need to manage the irrigation carefully when the fruit sets or it'll crack. I sell at roadside, usually can move it all by July.

Broccoli is new for me, only two years. I do a spring planting — transplant in early March, harvest by May before the cotton and maize rush. My cousin who farms in Shijiazhuang gave me the transplants last year. I'm still not sure about the right fertilizer rate, so I just follow what he does — 12 kg N or so.

Chili is small, just 7 mu, mostly family consumption and some local sales. Low effort crop.
